subject: Promptset acceptance & exception play — cross-functional asks for A/B rollout
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Gupta <priya.gupta@acme-labs.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Promptset acceptance & exception play — cross-functional asks for A/B rollout

Team —

Acme Labs ran a larger eval overnight against the promptset_v3 candidates and surfaced a handful of quality regressions vs. baseline on the customer-critical intents. They shared the eval snapshot (attached) and highlighted two high-priority failure modes: factual hallucination in policy-related answers and a drop in reranking precision for short queries.

We need to converge on an acceptance definition + an explicit exception/rollback play before the planned A/B deployment next week. Concretely I need the following by EOD Thu (2027-06-17):

- A concise acceptance checklist (metrics + thresholds) that the product/QA team can run automatically.
- An A/B traffic plan with canary percentages, monitoring windows, and owner for each gate.
- A clearly defined exception path: who approves an exception, what communication goes to the customer, and auto-rollback triggers if any.

Attachments: promptset_v3.csv (sample prompts + labels), eval_metrics_snapshot.json (Acme's run).

Notes / constraints:
- Latency must not increase > 10% p95 vs. current serving mode.
- We must avoid partial acceptance where hallucination is reduced but reranking drops more than 3pp.

Please reply with proposed thresholds and any open questions. I will coordinate the customer comms once we have the exception path.

Thanks,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Priya Gupta <priya.gupta@acme-labs.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Promptset acceptance & exception play — cross-functional asks for A/B rollout

Thanks Naomi — I reviewed Acme's eval snapshot and ran a short internal pass. High level proposal below (I kept it compact so you can paste into the customer-facing doc):

Proposed acceptance checklist (must all be green for acceptance):
- Intent-level accuracy (micro-F1) not less than baseline minus 1.5 points for core intents (policy, billing, auth flows).
- Hallucination rate on fact-based intents: <= 2.0% (measured by our hallucination-detector routine).
- Reranking precision@3: no more than 2.5 percentage points drop vs baseline.
- Latency: p95 increase <= 10% (Naomi already noted).
- Safety flags (policy triggers): no new false positives > 1% on production control set.

Metric definitions and how to measure: see attached eval_metrics_snapshot.json; I'll add our scoring script to the drive link. Use a rolling 1-hour window during canary for all early gates.

A/B traffic plan (canary stages):
- Stage 0: 0% (smoke in staging for 2h)
- Stage 1: 1% traffic for 30m — sanity checks + automated scoring (owner: Marissa)
- Stage 2: 5% traffic for 2h — extended scoring + production log inspection (owner: Marissa + CS)
- Stage 3: 20% for 4h — business metrics observed (owner: Jonas)
- Stage 4: 50% for 6h — final acceptance (owner: Jonas + Naomi)

Rollback / exception triggers (automated):
- If any acceptance metric breaches by >50% of the allowed delta (e.g., reranking drop >1.25pp beyond allowed) over the monitoring window, auto-rollback to baseline.
- If hallucination > 4% in any 30m window, auto-rollback.
- If latency p95 increases > 20%, auto-rollback.

Manual exception path (if we still want to hold despite breach):
- Escalation to Naomi (product) + Jonas (infra) + Marissa (quality).
- If approved, require a mitigation plan and customer notification within 2 business hours; maintain extra monitoring for 48h.

I'll attach a short ab_traffic_plan.xlsx with timings and dashboard panels. If everyone is aligned I can convert this into the formal runbook and the DocuSign customer notification template.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Applied ML / Evals

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Promptset acceptance & exception play — cross-functional asks for A/B rollout

Thanks — solid, Marissa. A couple of operational questions / asks before we lock this in: 

1) Cost/latency guardrail: the latency rule is fine, but we also need a per-token cost budget threshold during Stage 3/4. If cost per request rises > 12% vs baseline, we should surface to infra and finance and consider throttling. Can you add a cost column to the ab_traffic_plan?

2) Monitoring and ownership: who will be on-call during the initial 24h? Suggest: Jonas infra lead (primary), Karthik (secondary for routing), Marissa (quality triage). Please confirm.

3) Control prompts: add a 50-item control set (from promptset_v3) that runs against both candidates every 5m and reports diffs. If more than 6 control prompts flip sentiment/intent or hallucinate, trigger an alert. This should be automated.

4) Canary automation: we should make the rollback automated via the smart router so the route flips back with no human action when thresholds hit. Jonas — is this ready?

If everyone agrees I can add these items to the runbook and create the alert rules in PagerDuty/Grafana.

Cheers,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Engineering / Serving Runtime

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Priya Gupta <priya.gupta@acme-labs.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Promptset acceptance & exception play — cross-functional asks for A/B rollout

Quick status from infra/routing side:

- Smart router supports automated rollback based on metric webhooks — we already have a prototype for model-level canaries. I will deploy the canary policy for this rollout.
- On-call: Jonas (primary), Karthik (secondary), Naomi (notify). I'll add Marissa to the alert channel for quality metrics.
- Cost telemetry: I will surface per-request cost in the stage dashboards and add the 12% budget alert.

Suggested timelines (assuming approvals today):
- Wed 2027-06-16: staging smoke + control set run (2h)
- Thu 2027-06-17: Stage 1 & 2 (1% then 5%) — live monitoring and triage
- Fri 2027-06-18: Stage 3 (20%) — extended business metrics collection
- Mon 2027-06-21: Stage 4 (50%) and finalize decision

I uploaded a canary_playbook.pdf with wiring details and the dashboard links are in related_links. Priya — if Acme wants a separate notification cadence we can add an SLA-backed status page.

On the manual exception approval: please call out the minimum mitigation contents in the doc (root cause hypothesis + quick rollback plan + short-term mitigations) so customer comms are crisp.

-Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Promptset acceptance & exception play — cross-functional asks for A/B rollout

All right — this looks actionable. Summary of what I'll communicate to Acme and to execs:

- Acceptance checklist: the five Marissa metrics as written.
- Canary plan: Jonas timeline + Marissa ownership for stages 1–2, Jonas primary for 3–4.
- Auto-rollback triggers: Marissa's thresholds + Karthik's cost guardrail.
- Manual exception path: Naomi + Jonas + Marissa sign-off; customer notified within 2 business hours.

Action items:
- Marissa: drop the final ab_traffic_plan.xlsx into Drive and tag the doc owner (today).
- Jonas: enable smart-router rollback policy and add the cost alert (today).
- Karthik: create control-set alert rule and add to PagerDuty (today).
- Naomi: send customer-facing note to Priya with the high-level checklist and timeline after today's changes are in Drive (I'll send by 5pm PT).

Priya — we appreciate the Acme team surfacing this. We'll share the finalized runbook and keep you updated at each canary stage. Expect an email from me by 17:00 PT with the summary + link to the runbook.

Thanks everyone,
Naomi
